domain: DNA fragmentation, chromatin tagmentation, and restriction-associated library preparation
artifact_status: Proposed scientific rule content for review; not an admitted ontology, benchmark gold standard, or experimental validation

execution_scope.work_location: Local read-only source research and one new provenance artifact
execution_scope.coverage: Targeted inspection of the primary sections listed below. No full-paper or full-supplement coverage is claimed.
execution_scope.quotation_policy: No verbatim source quotations are stored. Source facts are paraphrased and linked.

frozen_local_contract.observable_input: Exact selected Operation IDs and their State interfaces, source-defined variant, inspected primary passages, proposed definition, and the intended granularity of comparison.
frozen_local_contract.scientific_target: A supported comparison of what physical transformation occurs, on which material, by which catalytic process, and with which retained product and information effect.
frozen_local_contract.separate_target: A proposed substitution must also connect the actual incoming material to the candidate operation and its outgoing material to the receiving workflow. Mechanism membership alone does not identify this feasibility.
invariants: Preserve source-specific material association, route, retained fraction, sample identity, and adapter attachment stage.
Do not invent a free-DNA intermediate where tagmentation acts on chromatin, or a ligase step where adapters enter by transposase strand transfer.
Keep unknowns distinct from supported absence and from contradiction.
Do not turn one supported component mechanism into an identity claim about an entire selected module.
success_criteria: Recover the Tn5 tagging family across ATAC, ChIPmentation and Nextera at an explicitly restricted reaction scope.
Preserve differences in chromatin association, upstream selection and information effect.
Reject tagging-versus-purification mechanism identity and Tn5-versus-restriction-plus-ligation mechanism identity at a catalytic transformation scope.
Expose missing adapter/end or retained-product facts when they are necessary to a proposed transfer.
not_identifiable_from_this_audit: General experimental interchangeability, equivalent yields or biases, universal buffer tolerances, new biological feasibility, historical descent, or novelty.
Exact sequence compatibility where commercial oligonucleotide or reagent compositions are undisclosed.

inspected_local_files: docs/EXTRACTION_SCOPE_AND_MATCHING.md (opening scope, gap, and matching sections)
existing_architecture.reuse: ComparisonProfile already separates State entity, form/association, identity/information, lineage and context from Operation transformation, purpose, mechanism, information effect and context. Put the checks below into those assertions and definition-specific review. Do not replace that architecture with a universal assay-stage list.
existing_architecture.implementation_boundary: Existing reported/inferred/unknown/not_assessed assertion statuses and evidence bindings should carry these domain questions. Proposed comparison and transfer outcomes below describe scientific review logic, not new graph relation names or a new schema.

sources.citation: Buenrostro et al. 2013, original ATAC-seq, doi:10.1038/nmeth.2688
accessed_sections: Author-manuscript Results: ATAC-seq probes chromatin accessibility with transposons; Figure 1 caption
Online Methods: prepare nuclei; transpose and purify; PCR; low cell number protocol; library QC and quantitation
Online Methods: primary data processing paragraph concerning 9-bp insertion geometry
sources.access_limits: PMC author-manuscript title differs from the final journal title but identifies the same DOI. Supplement download did not expose readable content and is not counted as inspected.

supported_facts.fact: Adapter-loaded hyperactive Tn5 fragments and tags DNA in unfixed nuclei; less accessible chromatin reduces insertion probability.
Standard preparation tagmented the nuclei pellet, then used MinElute purification and PCR. Low-cell preparations instead entered PCR without that purification.
Size selection was avoided to preserve complexity. Insert positions and lengths support chromatin interpretations.
The analysis describes paired adapter insertion separated by nine bases and adjusts read starts accordingly.

accessed_sections: Author-institution PDF, printed main-text pages 1-3: purified ChIP-DNA versus bead-bound chromatin comparison and stated limitations
Online Methods PDF page 4: standard ChIP-seq; ChIPmentation; ChIP-tagmentation with purified ChIP DNA; amplification and sequencing
sources.access_limits: PMC returned a browser challenge; Nature returned an inaccessible redirect. Author-institution PDF was readable. Supplementary Note detailing the three upstream ChIP protocols was not inspected.

supported_facts.fact: Tagmentation acts on immunoprecipitated bead-bound chromatin before elution, cross-link reversal and DNA purification.
Pre-reaction washes remove detergent, salts and EDTA; the reaction contains magnesium. Post-reaction bead washes precede resumed ChIP processing.
Purified ChIP-DNA tagmentation was more sensitive to DNA/transposase ratio. Authors proposed chromatin protein protection and reported greater robustness on beads.
The comparison standard ChIP-seq route used end repair, A-tailing and T4-ligase adapter attachment. ChIPmentation used Nextera enzyme and custom Nextera PCR primers.
Low-input performance still depended on antibody quality and was not established for every target.

sources.citation: Adey et al. 2010, high-density in vitro transposition library construction, doi:10.1186/gb-2010-11-12-r119
accessed_sections: Background: ME-containing transposome and synthetic-adapter explanation
Materials and methods: genomic DNA; mechanical shearing; enzymatic fragmentation; post-fragmentation library preparation; transposase-based library preparation
Materials and methods: PCR-free library construction paragraphs concerning adapter assembly and nick translation
Results: exome-capture paragraph concerning custom adapter-blocking oligonucleotides
sources.access_limits: Targeted sections only; additional files were not inspected. Reported protocols contain some numerical/textual irregularities, so this audit does not reproduce an execution recipe.

supported_facts.fact: Tn5 complexes use mosaic-end DNA; separate synthetic ME adapters yield fragmentation with adapter joining to target-DNA 5-prime ends. Limited PCR appends platform sequences.
A PCR-free variant instead incorporated platform sequences in loaded oligonucleotides and used nick translation.
The paper separately implemented sonication, Fragmentase, and transposase library routes.
Different adapter sequences required custom blocking oligonucleotides during exome capture.

sources.citation: Illumina Nextera DNA Library Prep Reference Guide, document 15027987 v01, January 2016
accessed_sections: Printed pages 2-3: introduction and DNA input recommendations
Printed pages 9-12: tagment genomic DNA; cleanup of tagmented DNA; amplification overview
Printed page 15: library cleanup overview
Printed page 23: assay mechanism overview
sources.access_limits: Version-specific manufacturer specification, not a universal statement about Tn5 variants or all Nextera products. No undisclosed reagent composition is inferred.

supported_facts.fact: Engineered transposome fragments and tags genomic DNA; subsequent PCR adds indices, P5/P7 and sequencing-related sequences.
For this assay, ssDNA, RNA and free oligonucleotides are not target substrates.
Transposome removal prevents DNA-end binding from interfering with subsequent processing. Later bead cleanup removes short library fragments.
The guide cautions that tagmentation cannot place adapters at distal pre-existing fragment ends and that DNA input affects the enzymatic fragmentation.

sources.citation: Baird et al. 2008, sequenced RAD markers, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0003376
accessed_sections: Results: RAD marker generation for sequencing; Figure 1 caption
Methods: isolation of RAD markers for Illumina sequencing
sources.access_limits: Targeted library-construction sections; mapping analyses and supplemental data not audited.

supported_facts.fact: EcoRI or SbfI cleavage precedes T4-ligase attachment of P1, which supplies sample barcode and amplification/sequencing interfaces.
P1-ligated samples are pooled, randomly sheared and size-selected; polished ends are A-tailed before P2 attachment.
P2 is divergent; productive reverse-primer binding follows forward extension from P1. This selectively amplifies P1-containing fragments.
Published P1 designs distinguish EcoRI and SbfI overhang polarity and include phosphorylated oligonucleotides.

accessed_sections: Methods: Double Digest Restriction Associated DNA Sequencing
Methods: Sample Multiplexing via Combinatorial Indexing
Supporting information descriptions identifying Protocol S1 and Sequences S1
sources.access_limits: Targeted architecture sections; analytical performance sections and oligonucleotide spreadsheet were not fully inspected.

supported_facts.fact: Double restriction digestion replaces random shearing and end repair. Libraries select fragments with one end from each enzyme and within the size window.
Inline sample barcodes enter by adapter ligation before pooling; a second index enters during pooled-library PCR.
Restriction choice and size selection jointly control the genomic subset represented.

sources.citation: Peterson et al. 2012, Protocol S1, detailed ddRADseq laboratory protocol
accessed_sections: Primary protocol reproduced as 7-page PDF: definitions; materials; adapter annealing; double digest; adapter ligation
Pooling before size selection; size selection; optional streptavidin removal; PCR
Appendix 1: oligonucleotide-end and overhang design notes
sources.access_limits: Official PLOS .doc download failed via an expired/inaccessible signed redirect. The accessed document is an academic-site mirror of the primary supplement, not a new independent study. Its bytes were not matched to the inaccessible official .doc. Cost appendix not audited.

supported_facts.fact: Annealed P1/P2 adapters are joined to digested DNA using T4 ligase; both enzymes require an appropriate shared digestion buffer.
EcoRI/MspI adapter designs accommodate their 5-prime overhangs; SbfI substitution changes the oligonucleotide strand carrying the 3-prime overhang.
Flexible adapters can accept SphI or NlaIII products, and EcoRI or MluCI products, despite different recognition-site lengths.
P1/P1 products can amplify but do not form the desired sequencing clusters; optional biotinylated P2 permits their depletion. PCR completes other sequencing interfaces.

accessed_sections: Manufacturer search-result excerpt for the T4 DNA Ligase Products section
sources.access_limits: Auxiliary chemistry confirmation only. Full catalog fetch exceeded the web reader size limit and the product page timed out; no full-section or full-catalog inspection is claimed.

supported_facts.fact: T4 DNA ligase joins adjacent 5-prime phosphate and 3-prime hydroxyl termini, including cohesive/blunt substrates and nicks in specified duplex contexts.

proposed_rules.name: Declare what must be identical before comparison
necessary_checks: Name the selected reaction or connected path and its exact incoming/outgoing states.
State whether the assertion concerns catalytic chemistry, a contextual material transformation, a genomic selection strategy, or an entire assay/module.
List which interfaces and information effects the definition includes; retain excluded differences explicitly as context.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: A shared broad chemistry can be true while a more specific transformation definition fails. Do not resolve an overly specific failed definition by silently dropping its consequential qualifiers.

proposed_rules.name: Read the actual substrate and association
necessary_checks: Record duplex versus single-strand target, free versus nucleoprotein-associated DNA, native versus processed chromatin, bead association, and any prior fragmentation or enrichment when consequential to the asserted scope.
Determine whether access to DNA is itself the measured selection or only a constraint on library construction.
Use documented substrate presentation, not the reagent's name, to establish applicability. Restrict a manufacturer substrate statement to its exact assay/version.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: Different association can fit a broad Tn5 family yet contradict a definition requiring native-nuclear accessibility probing. An unreported association blocks only claims that need it. RNA use cannot be excluded merely from a reagent being called DNA ligase.

proposed_rules.name: Discriminate the catalytic action
necessary_checks: For tagmentation, establish an active adapter-loaded transposome, recognition-end-bearing oligonucleotides, target fragmentation and covalent adapter strand transfer within the selected reaction.
For restriction plus ligation, distinguish sequence-directed cleavage from subsequent ligase-mediated joining at existing fragment ends.
For a composite selection, identify each constituent process; shared use of one enzyme does not cover other selected transformations.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: Tn5 tagging and restriction-plus-T4 ligation can share a library-generation purpose. They fail identity at the fragmentation-and-attachment mechanism scope. They may share only an explicitly coarser joining category, which cannot be used to transfer a reaction recipe.

proposed_rules.name: Check end chemistry independently of labels
necessary_checks: For a ligation handoff, compare overhang sequence, polarity, terminal phosphate/hydroxyl availability, duplex geometry and required preparation. Use actual adapter designs; a matching adapter label is insufficient.
For a tagmentation handoff, do not substitute the assumption of fully repaired duplex ends for the source's tagged intermediate and subsequent completion step.
Record pre-existing fragment ends and fragment-length constraints if the claim requires tagging or recovering those ends.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: An explicitly mismatched cohesive end contradicts the proposed direct sticky-end transfer until a supported conversion is added. Unknown end chemistry leaves that handoff unresolved. Adapter-compatible ends support a local interface, not identity of the enzyme's genomic selector.

proposed_rules.name: Track oligonucleotide function and attachment time
necessary_checks: Separate the transposase recognition end, amplification handle, sequencing-primer interface, platform/cluster interface, sample barcode and affinity handle. A single oligonucleotide can carry several functions.
Record whether each function enters through loaded-adapter strand transfer, end ligation, primer extension/PCR, or affinity labeling.
Check whether downstream primers or capture blockers recognize the actual resulting sequences and whether the desired combination occurs on a recoverable molecule.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: Same broad catalytic mechanism can tolerate different payloads. Functional output identity or transfer requires the necessary payload and downstream recognition. A transposition product is not automatically a completed indexed, cluster-ready library.

proposed_rules.name: Preserve the retained product and genomic ascertainment
necessary_checks: Identify which material is retained through each cleanup, bead separation, elution and size gate.
Distinguish DNA merely fragmented, covalently tagged, amplifiable, and capable of producing the intended sequencing readout.
For reduced representation, record recognition-site requirements, one versus two restriction-defined ends, and the size-selection rule.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: A change in retained genomic subset contradicts identity at an ascertainment-specific scope even if the enzyme family is shared. Amplification alone does not prove the intended final adapter combination. A cleanup mechanism is separate from an adapter-tagging mechanism.

proposed_rules.name: Treat conditions according to their causal role and evidence
necessary_checks: Retain reported temperature, duration, substrate/enzyme amounts, buffer/cofactor state, inhibitors, washing, quenching and downstream release/completion steps for the actual variant.
Ask whether a difference changes catalytic family, changes the selected substrate/product, or only leaves performance/compatibility untested.
For transfer, require support for the candidate reaction in the actual incoming matrix or a documented conversion; matching a few numerical conditions is insufficient.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: Condition differences alone neither refute a shared catalytic family nor prove transfer. An omitted condition is blocking only when the asserted scope or proposed handoff depends on it. No universal temperature, concentration, fragment-size or cleanup-equality threshold follows from these papers.

proposed_rules.name: Separate common mechanism from measurement identity
necessary_checks: Describe which pre-existing biological property is selected or read out and which identities are preserved, introduced or lost.
Keep sample lineage, upstream antibody selection and native accessibility separate from downstream adapter addition.
Do not infer a biological footprint or an unbiased genomic representation merely from common tagmentation chemistry.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: A general adapter-generation purpose may span distinct mechanisms. A common Tn5 catalytic family can span different measurement purposes. Neither relation establishes identical information effects.

proposed_rules.name: Judge substitution on directed interfaces
necessary_checks: Write the proposed donor operation, recipient input state, required output state and all planned conversions.
Evaluate substrate access, catalytic inputs, oligonucleotide/end compatibility, retained product and downstream completion/recognition separately.
Distinguish a directly demonstrated substitution in a stated context from a chemically plausible interface and from an untested condition change.
proposed_rules.decision_effect: A transfer is incompatible as proposed only where an explicit required interface is contradicted and no supported conversion is included. Otherwise missing consequential evidence yields unknown. A shared-mechanism edge supplies precedent; it supplies no general experimental interchangeability claim.

decision_sequence: Bind the comparison to exact selections, source variant and explicit definition granularity.
Assess purpose separately; it cannot answer a mechanism question.
Check the catalytic/material invariant required by that definition, preserving contextual differences.
If only a proper broader mechanism family fits, propose that family explicitly or report the narrower membership as unsupported/contradicted; never silently weaken the definition.
If a necessary fact is absent or inaccessible, record that exact unknown rather than treating it as equality or inequality.
Only for a requested transfer, evaluate the directed interfaces and distinguish documented demonstration, candidate feasibility, unknown and incompatible-as-proposed.

cases.comparison: Selected Tn5 fragmentation/tagging reactions in ATAC, ChIPmentation and Nextera
cases.declared_scope: Adapter-loaded Tn5 fragmentation with covalent adapter integration into DNA
cases.expected_judgment: Shared mechanism family supported by cross-source inference; contextual reaction and assay identity remain different.

cases.comparison: Tagmentation versus restriction digestion followed by adapter ligation
cases.expected_judgment: Common library-generation purpose; different catalytic transformations.

cases.comparison: RAD P1 attachment versus RAD P2 attachment
cases.declared_scope: Adapter attachment to the same end state with the same functional outcome
cases.expected_judgment: Both involve ligation, but overhang preparation, timing and amplification role prevent this narrower identity.

cases.comparison: Flexible ddRAD adapter used with SphI versus NlaIII
cases.declared_scope: Local ligation interface versus genomic restriction selector
cases.expected_judgment: The reported adapter interface can be shared while the genomic selection differs. Supplement-copy provenance qualification applies.

cases.comparison: Original ATAC standard versus low-cell route
cases.expected_judgment: Different pre-PCR cleanup does not refute the shared tagging mechanism. Preserve the route-specific interface.

cases.comparison: Single tagging reaction versus tagging plus transposome removal plus PCR
cases.declared_scope: Entire selected path has one shared tagging mechanism
cases.expected_judgment: Reject that whole-selection claim; only its tagging constituent fits. Do not add invented intermediates to force alignment.

cases.comparison: Directly substitute an EcoRI-end P1 adapter onto a SbfI-cleaved substrate without redesign or end conversion
cases.expected_judgment: The explicit end interface is contradicted. This is a failure of the proposed direct route, not proof that no redesigned route could work.

cases.comparison: Move a purified-DNA tagmentation recipe directly onto immunoprecipitated bead-bound chromatin
cases.declared_scope: Same chemistry implies the same usable operating conditions and output
cases.expected_judgment: Shared Tn5 family is supported; arbitrary condition transfer is unresolved. The paper's actual adapted bead protocol is a precedent, not evidence for every recipe.

cases.comparison: PCR-appended platform sequences versus PCR-free loaded platform sequences
cases.declared_scope: Tn5 tagging family versus completed-library transformation
cases.expected_judgment: Tagging family can be shared while platform completion enters at a different stage. The downstream handoff must name the actual product.

cases.comparison: ddRAD P1/P1 versus P1/P2 adapter combinations
cases.expected_judgment: PCR amplification is insufficient to assert the desired sequencing output; verify the retained adapter combination. Supplement-copy provenance qualification applies.

cases.comparison: Transfer a reported adapter-ligation operation to an extracted state labeled only fragmented DNA
cases.expected_judgment: Unknown until the required overhang/terminal/duplex interface is supported. Do not invent blunt ends, A-tails or phosphorylation.

cases.comparison: Single-enzyme RAD and ddRAD complete library paths
cases.expected_judgment: A broader restriction-associated reduced-representation family is shared; random-sheared second ends versus two restriction-defined ends defeats this narrower identity.

audit_limits: These are curator-designed necessary checks for declared claims, not universally sufficient experimental compatibility rules.
A numeric tolerance is not supplied for buffer, temperature, substrate amount, enzyme loading or fragment-size differences. Reported conditions are source-specific observations.

Tn5 specificity, enzyme variation, methylation sensitivity, terminal damage and matrix effects need targeted primary evidence when a proposed definition or transfer depends on them; they were not exhaustively audited here.
Commercial reagent names do not disclose every loaded oligonucleotide or enzyme composition. Do not promote inferred identity to directly reported molecular detail.

The primary ddRAD supplement was inspected through an academic mirror with explicit provenance limitations; acquire and verify the official supplement before using its exact sequences for an execution claim.

The NEB chemistry excerpt is auxiliary and openly marked as such; obtain the full specification or primary biochemical study if an adjudication depends on a substrate configuration beyond the inspected protocol evidence.
No source here establishes general interchangeability across ATAC, ChIPmentation, Nextera or RAD/ddRAD. Reported successful protocols establish bounded precedents.
No software tests, biological experiments or fresh model-admission runs were performed. This artifact does not validate extraction accuracy or matching performance.
